fields.meta_description: Build a legal intake form that counts the days to a filing deadline and sends each matter to the right attorney. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Legal Intake Form That Screens Matters Before a Consult
fields.hero_description: Describe the matters your firm takes and the answers that change who sees them first. Emergent builds the legal intake form and the database behind it.
fields.features_heading: What Goes Into a Legal Intake Form
fields.features_subheading: Each field gives an attorney something to act on before the first call.
fields.feature_1:
A disclaimer the visitor must check

Open the form with your firm's own wording, such as a line saying that submitting it does not make the visitor a client. A required checkbox records that they read it, with the time.
fields.feature_2:
Every party named in its own field

Ask for the other side's name and their lawyer's name, each in a separate field. Your staff then search the conflict list on clean names, not a paragraph someone has to read first.
fields.feature_3:
Dates that count the days for you

Ask for the date that starts the clock, such as a firing or a hearing. The form counts the days on submit and saves the number with the intake. Staff can sort the whole queue by it.
fields.feature_4:
Uploads filed with the matter

Let people upload a lease, a signed contract, a court notice or photos taken on a phone. Each file is saved in storage you own, filed under the intake it came with, ready for review.
fields.feature_5:
Questions that change by matter type

Ask the type of matter first and show only the questions that fit it. A landlord dispute asks about the lease and the rent owed, and a business dispute asks for the contract instead.
fields.feature_6:
Source code your firm keeps

Export the form and its database to your GitHub on paid plans. Host it on your firm's own servers, or have a developer connect it to the practice software your staff already use.

fields.usecase_heading: Legal Intake Forms by Practice Setting
fields.tab_content_1:
162 days in, and the attorney sees it the same afternoon

Talbot Employment Law asks prospective clients for the date they were fired. Renee Walsh was let go 162 days ago. The firm flags any intake past day 150, since an EEOC charge is due within 180 days in states without their own fair employment agency. Daniel Okoro gets hers in Slack that afternoon.
fields.tab_content_2:
Who qualifies is settled by household size

Eastgate Legal Aid takes households below 125% of the federal poverty guidelines, the cap for clinics the Legal Services Corporation funds. Carla Mendes enters a household of 3 on $2,450 a month and joins the housing queue on submit. Applicants over the line see reduced-fee referral options.
fields.tab_content_3:
$84,000 disputes go straight to a partner

A food distributor tells Kessler Ward, a business litigation firm, that a grocery chain owes it $84,000 in unpaid invoices. The supply contract and each invoice come in as uploads. Disputes over $50,000 go to partner Helen Ortiz with the files attached. An associate offers smaller ones a flat-fee demand letter.
fields.tab_content_4:
Only matters the firm handles reach its attorneys

Corbin Hale Law handles leases and business formation, and its intake opens with the type of matter. Pick a lease, and the lease questions open. Pick a traffic ticket, and the form ends with the county's lawyer referral service. Nothing lands in the attorneys' queue.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Legal Intake Form
fields.howto_description: Work backward from the first phone call, then decide which answers should move a matter before anyone calls back.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Print your current intake sheet, or write down what an attorney asks on a first call. Cross out anything nobody uses to decide whether to take the matter. What remains is the core of the online form, and a shorter form gets finished.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Group the questions by what they decide. Contact details come first, then the type of matter, then the facts that only matter for that type. A visitor with an employment claim should never scroll past questions written for a real estate closing.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Ask for every person and company involved, including the other side's lawyer if there is one. Put each name in its own field. Staff need clean names to search the firm's conflict list before anyone reads the facts of the matter.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Note each answer that should change what happens next, like a hearing within 14 days or an amount over a set figure. For each one, name the attorney who hears about it, by Slack or by email, and what the visitor sees after submitting.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Paste the questions and the rules into the prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it, and the alerts. When the firm adds a practice area later, prompt again and the live form changes to match.
fields.howto_step_6_des: End with the wording your firm uses about what submitting the form does and does not do, followed by a required checkbox. Have an attorney at the firm approve that wording before the form goes on the website.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Before the link goes on your website, submit a matter the firm takes and one it refers out. Then submit one with a close deadline. Check that each alert reaches the right attorney and that the referral page appears.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is printable intake sheets (a clinic at Harvard, an immigrant legal aid PDF, a Practical Law employment template), two Jotform template pages, a practice-management blog and a document-assembly site. Every one of them collects the same contact, matter and opposing-party questions and then stops. This page treats the legal intake form as triage: the answers decide, before an attorney spends time on the matter, whether a filing deadline is close, whether the person qualifies for a free clinic, which lawyer should see it and whether the firm takes that kind of matter at all. Four settings show that decision: an employment firm counting days toward the EEOC deadline, a legal aid clinic screening household income, a business litigation firm routing large contract disputes to a partner, and a general practice firm sending matters it does not handle to the county bar's referral line.
tab_stories: A fired warehouse supervisor enters her last day of work on an employment firm's intake, the form counts 162 days since then, and because the firm flags anything past day 150 of the 180-day EEOC window, the intake reaches the attorney the same afternoon.

A tenant applying to a legal aid clinic enters a household of 3 and a monthly income of $2,450, the form checks it against the clinic's 125% poverty-guideline limit, and she is placed in the housing queue instead of being sent a referral list.

A distributor describes an $84,000 unpaid-invoice dispute and uploads the supply contract, and because the firm sends disputes over $50,000 to a partner, the intake lands with partner Helen Ortiz with the contract attached.

A visitor to a general practice firm picks a traffic ticket as the matter type, the firm does not handle traffic cases, so the form ends at the county's referral line and nothing enters the attorneys' queue.
